questions.answer: The folds give a huge surface area for respiratory enzymes, so more aerobic respiration and more ATP production can happen.
questions.explanation: Scene s1 shows cristae folding the inner membrane: folding means huge surface area, so more ATP is made.
questions.prompt: Explain why the folded cristae of a mitochondrion help it make more ATP.

questions.answer: Yeast: ethanol + carbon dioxide. Muscle: lactic acid. Both yield far less ATP than aerobic respiration because glucose is only partly broken down.
questions.explanation: Scene s4 forks one glucose two ways: yeast to ethanol + CO2, muscle to lactic acid, with far less ATP than aerobic either way.
questions.prompt: Compare anaerobic respiration in yeast and in muscle: name the products of each and state the ATP yield compared with aerobic respiration.
